subject: Procurement sequencing and parallel review plan for CureLytics pilot
messages:
From: Elena Martell <elena.martell@curelytics.com>

Cc: procurement@curelytics.com
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 09:13:11 -0700
Subject: CureLytics pilot: RFP details and timing

Hi Sergio,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the inference latency numbers. Procurement asked me to send over the RFP and a rough ask on timeline so they can map legal and PO timing to our internal quarter close. Attached is our RFP and the procurement constraints we need to follow.

High level asks:
- We need confirmation of the contract sequence (MSA -> DPA -> Order Form?) and whether any items can be parallelized.
- SOC 2 artifact availability and a runbook for acceptance testing tied to the order form.
- Target commercial close before 2027-06-15 to align with budget window.

Can you propose a mutual action plan (MAP) with milestone owners + dates? If Redwood can parallel DPA and legal review we might be able to hit the 6/15 target.

Attached: CureLytics-RFP.pdf

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Martell
Head of Procurement, CureLytics
procurement@curelytics.com

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 11:02:45 -0700
Subject: Re: CureLytics pilot: RFP details and timing

Thanks Elena — copied Grace (CS lead) and Karthik (legal). I pulled together an initial MAP draft that maps procurement and legal sequencing and highlights what we can parallelize. See summary below and I attached the MAP workbook.

Quick answers up front:
- Preferred sequencing: sign MSA (master commercial terms) -> sign DPA (data protection) concurrently with security artifact delivery -> finalize & sign Order Form.
- We can run MSA and DPA reviews in parallel for redlines, but the Order Form (purchase details and billing) will require an executed MSA at close for our internal billing workflow. Practically that means we can push towards a 6/11 close if redlines are reasonable and SOC2 artifacts are already accessible to your team.

Proposed MAP (high level):
1) 2027-05-25: Redwood sends MAP v1 + redlines guidance (owner: Sergio)
2) 2027-05-26 to 2027-05-31: CureLytics legal & procurement review MSA/DPA in parallel (owner: Elena / CureLytics legal)
3) 2027-06-01: Exchange consolidated redlines (owner: both legal teams)
4) 2027-06-02 to 2027-06-07: Redwood legal finalizes MSA/DPA; Security provides SOC2 evidence + acceptance runbook (owner: Karthik + Grace)
5) 2027-06-08: Final sign & countersign MSA/DPA; Redwood issues Order Form for signature (owner: procurement teams)
6) 2027-06-09 to 2027-06-11: Order Form execution + PO processing (target close window)

Key blockers we need from your side:
- SOC2 report (or temporary SOC2 access to our security team)
- Procurement term exceptions list (attach any mandatory PO language)
- Decision owner for PO approval (name + timeline)

I attached \"Redwood-MAP-draft_v1.xlsx\" with a lane-by-lane breakdown and owners. If that sequence works I can lock dates and create a shared Drive folder and a HubSpot plan link.

Attachments: Redwood-MAP-draft_v1.xlsx

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com
(415) 555-0131

From: Elena Martell <elena.martell@curelytics.com>

Sergio — appreciate the fast turnaround and the MAP. A couple of clarifications from procurement/legal:
- Can Redwood accept our standard PO terms? We have two mandatory clauses around indemnity cap and payment net-60 that are non-negotiable.
- SOC2: we can provide the latest report, but procurement will need a short summary of the controls mapped to the pilot scope (who can produce that from Redwood?).
- Our legal wants to see a redlines_summary.pdf after the first pass (so they can triage must-haves).

Also looping in David (IT security) to coordinate artifact access. If Redwood can provide the SOC2 mapping + a short technical runbook for acceptance tests by Friday (05/28), we'll kick legal review immediately.

Attached: procurement-terms.docx

Thanks,
Elena

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 09:46:22 -0700
Subject: Re: CureLytics pilot: RFP details and timing

Sergio / Grace — quick legal take and sequencing constraints:

1) MSA vs DPA: we can absolutely review both in parallel and exchange redlines, but for commercial activation (sending invoices and processing PO) our platform requires the MSA to be executed first. For most customers we've run DPA parallel and then completed signature after MSA countersignature when necessary.

2) Indemnity / net-60: we'll need procurement to identify whether the indemnity cap is a hard requirement or a risk-based ask. Net-60 payment terms are longer than our standard; we can accept extended payment terms with an accelerated invoice/acceptance milestone (e.g., acceptance triggers invoice start).

3) Evidence & SOC2 mapping: Grace — can your team produce a 1-page controls mapping and a short acceptance-runbook by EOD Friday 05/28? If yes, we can feed that into the MAP and that materially reduces legal friction.

4) Redlines summary: once we receive CureLytics' redlines we will produce a \"redlines_summary.pdf\" that separates critical vs negotiable items to speed exec approvals.

I will be available for a 30-min legal sync on 05/28 afternoon (tentative).

-Karthik
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com

- CureLytics legal sends consolidated redlines by 06/01 (owner: CureLytics legal)

Sergio
